name: Primacist Hawks
overview: The Primacist Hawks argue that American safety rests on American primacy: hostile regimes that take hostages, sponsor proxies and seek the bomb are removed or broken, not managed (Maduro is gone; Tehran is next); allies that fight their own wars, Israel first, multiply US power; China is denied the chips that would close the gap; Russia stays under sanctions. Credibility is one account, so retreat on one front invites tests on every other. In their own terms this is Reagan's peace through strength, and restraint is what invites war.

The interest layer is a donor network that funds the Republican majorities and disciplines dissent. Miriam Adelson gave at least $67.6M in 2025-26 ($25M MAGA Inc., $30M Senate Leadership Fund, $10M CLF); Paul Singer was the largest donor to the anti-Massie MAGA KY and America 21 ($3M) and gave AIPAC's United Democracy Project its largest individual gift ($2.5M). Pro-Gallrein groups spent about $15.5M and Massie lost (May 19). The Marcus Foundation's $19M to FDD supplies staff and arguments. Defense primes gain from the program (Lockheed's $35B THAAD deal; RTX's $289B backlog), but no contractor payment to the hawk core was found. For Rubio and Cruz the network is the 2028 base; for the Florida delegation it is the exile vote.

Acts depart from words where Trump decides. When Trump signed the June Iran deal, Adelson's Israel Hayom called him a failure (Jun 19) and Levin accused officials of bullying Israel, while the RJC urged trust in Trump (Jun 18) and Rubio sold the deal and told allies there would be no new strikes 'for now' (Aug 25). The access wing follows Trump; the Israel-first wing pushes and loses rounds. On aid the program and the patron diverge: Netanyahu wants US grants phased out ('start now', Jun 3), which per lesson L1 frees Israel from end-use strings while the US still underwrites the war; FDD wants it slow (Jun 9), which protects the purchases and the leverage (my reading).

Precedent: the 2002-03 coalition of think tanks, donors and officials that carried the Iraq war. It breaks in three places: then the hawks held the vice-presidency and the Pentagon's civilian leadership, now Trump runs the clock and the Pentagon's own interest is restocking; then the right's media were with them, now its largest audience (Carlson) is against them; and Rubio is no Cheney, because his career depends on following, not steering (my reading).

Why the faction does it. The worldview: Tehran's regime is the hub of the proxies and the bomb, and a deal only buys it time. The interest: the donor network that funds the majorities (Adelson, Singer, the RJC, AIPAC's UDP) and an Israeli government that wants the US in the fight but out of its decisions.

Rubio. Posture: skeptic of the deal, for donors and Florida. Interest: Trump's favor and 2028; he executes whatever Trump decides (documented acts).
Cruz. Posture: the war's loudest Senate defender ('anti-American propaganda', Mar 10). Interest: a 2028 lane built on the pro-Israel network; no 2026 payment to him found.
Adelson. Her paper called the June deal a 'surrender' and Trump a failure (Jun 19). She is the faction's biggest patron and lost that round.

Netanyahu. Posture: partner. Interest: freedom of action. He wants US grants phased out ('start now', Jun 3). Trump's Nov 3 claim that aid 'gets cut off' is a claim, with no act shown.
Say versus do. The donor wing says strike; the faction's officials execute Trump's hold. Its real wins on Iran come through Israel's freedom to act and Congress, not the decision.

Stance audit. Rubio reportedly doubted the June agreement, then defended it and signaled a pause on new strikes. The June 15 and August 25 accounts span different phases of policy. Public advocacy for the deal is an observable change in posture. Loyalty and succession standing can reward defending Trump. Adelson and other pro-Israel backers give parts of the faction electoral leverage. Strategic accommodation is plausible. A change in Rubio’s private view or a donor instruction remains unresolved.

Cruz Motives: (1) Ambition: pro-Israel donors are the coalition a 2028 run needs; his feud with Carlson over the war (Mar 10) is a pitch to them, and RJC CEO Matt Brooks said such moves are 'definitely getting noticed' (Axios, Nov 2025). (2) Money: his podcast raises small-dollar money. (3) The Iran lane separates him from Vance. Griffin Motives: Patronage: predisposed to Rubio (reported). No amount found.

Nov 7 nominee/faction consistency review: Rubio’s war defense and Cruz’s competing lane must be assessed separately; overlapping hawk networks cannot be counted as exclusive support for both. Rubio follows Trump in some disputes even when other hawks dissent. His public deferral to Vance and Nov 5 denial of campaign-related departure constrain entry assumptions.
